title: Ada and the Oath
premise: Isandro Dunmore, a royal food-taster who poisons herself in small doses to stay useful and invisible, secretly keeps the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things, which trades in memories, oaths, and other intangibles. When a dying stranger presses a map of the buried Oathstone into her hands, she becomes the unwilling bearer of a secret that could shatter the peace sealed three centuries ago between humans and the vanished fae. Hunted by the Crown's spymaster, courted by the guild's enigmatic master Corvane, and haunted by fragments of memory that are not her own, Isandro must choose between delivering the stone to those who would weaponize it or destroying it and losing every trace of the mother she never knew. In the end she breaks the Oath itself—unbinding the fae from exile—at the cost of her own recorded existence, vanishing from all ledgers but alive, finally belonging to no one's ledger but her own.
about_author: J. M. Vane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing guild records in coastal trading towns before turning to fiction. They write about people who keep secrets for a living and live quietly off the page.

chapters.title: The Taster's Portion
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She swallows a suspect broth at the royal table, catalogs its toxins with clinical calm, and slips afterward to the guildhall to enter the evening's trades in the ledgers. The beat establishes her double life: meticulous, invisible, and quietly starving for something she won't name.

chapters.title: Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She balances the guild's books—memories sold by the vial, oaths pawned against futures—and notices an entry in her dead mother's handwriting dated three days from now. The emotional beat is unease blooming into obsession; the impossible has entered her own accounts.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Salt Gate
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A bleeding stranger corners her on the docks, presses a wax-sealed map into her hands, and dies whispering the word 'Oathkeeper.' She flees as city watch approach. The beat is terror and reluctant responsibility—the moment invisibility ends.

chapters.title: What the Poison Teaches
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At court she tastes for the queen while mentally decoding the map, realizing the Oathstone lies beneath the palace itself. Spymaster Lady Vess watches her too closely. The beat is claustrophobic tension: the danger is under her feet and across the table.

chapters.title: Corvane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Guildmaster Corvane reveals he knows she has the map and offers protection—for a price: her oldest memory, the face of the woman who raised her. The beat is temptation and first real intimacy, as he is the only person who has ever truly seen her.

chapters.title: The Queen's Hunger
chapters.summary: Queen Maren's POV. The queen, slowly poisoned by her own council, suspects her taster knows more than she tastes. She interrogates Isandro gently, almost kindly. The beat is unexpected kinship between two women kept as instruments by the same machine.

chapters.title: Ink That Remembers
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Testing the ledger's strange ink, she discovers entries rewrite themselves when oaths are broken—and finds her own name appearing in a ledger she never opened. The beat is dread: someone has been writing her life before she lives it.

chapters.title: Down the Stair of Teeth
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Following the map through palace cellars, she finds the sealed stair to the Oathstone chamber and a door that opens only to fae blood—her blood. The beat is revelation and vertigo: her immunity was never trained, it was inherited.

chapters.title: Vess Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Lady Vess's POV. The spymaster arrests the guildhall staff and burns half the ledgers, hunting the map. Her chapters reveal she broke the original Oath's terms once before. The beat is cold ambition shadowed by old guilt.

chapters.title: A Memory Not Mine
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A stolen vial of memory floods her with her mother's final night: the Oath being forged, a child smuggled out, a promise made to the fae. The beat is grief transformed into purpose—she now knows what the stone truly holds.

chapters.title: The Price of Seeing
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Cornered by Vess's agents, she is saved by Corvane, who takes a blade meant for her. Healing him, she admits she loves him—and refuses his bargain anyway. The beat is love declared against duty, choosing feeling over safety.

chapters.title: Halfway to Exile
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She flees the city with the map sewn into her coat, guided by the queen's secret seal. Vess declares her traitor; the guild brands her oathbreaker. The beat is loneliness sharpened into resolve on the open road.

chapters.title: The Fae Who Waited
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. In the border marshes she meets Serevan, a fae exile who has guarded the outer road for three centuries waiting for 'the daughter of the ledger-keeper.' The beat is wonder and belonging—the first place she is expected rather than tolerated.

chapters.title: Terms of the Old Peace
chapters.summary: Serevan's POV. He recounts the true history: the Oath didn't banish the fae—it caged them to stop a war both sides started, and the stone is the lock and the key. The beat is moral complexity; destroying the stone may free a people or unleash a slaughter.

chapters.title: Vess at the Ford
chapters.summary: Lady Vess's POV. Vess intercepts them, revealing she wants the stone not for the Crown but to resurrect someone the Oath cost her. She offers Isandro her mother's fate in exchange for the map. The beat is a mirror: two women bargaining with grief.

chapters.title: What Isandro Owes
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Reading the rewritten ledger one last time, she sees the entry in her mother's hand is her own death notice, dated tomorrow. She accepts that some debts are paid forward, not escaped. The beat is quiet acceptance before the storm.

chapters.title: Return to the Palace
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She walks back into the capital openly, using her taster's credentials to reach the queen, and exposes the council's slow poisoning. The queen grants her one hour beneath the palace. The beat is courage—the invisible woman making herself unmistakable.

chapters.title: The Chamber of the Stone
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. With Corvane, Serevan, and Vess all converging, she reaches the Oathstone and hears every voice ever bound inside it—including her mother's. The beat is overwhelming communion; the stone offers her everything if she only keeps it whole.

chapters.title: Breaking the Oath
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. Vess attacks, Corvane chooses Isandro over the guild, and Isandro shatters the stone with her own fae blood, unbinding the exiles and erasing every ledger entry written in oath-ink—including hers. The climax beat is sacrifice: she saves everyone by deleting herself.

chapters.title: Names Unwritten
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. In the aftermath, the freed fae depart peacefully; Vess, broken, turns herself in. Corvane searches the surviving ledgers and finds no trace of Isandro anywhere—except one line in his own heart's memory that no ink can touch. The beat is mourning without a grave.

chapters.title: The Taster Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Alive but unwritten, she wakes in the marshes where Serevan tends her; the stone's destruction spent her name, not her life. She tastes rainwater like a feast. The beat is rebirth—belonging at last to no record but her own.

chapters.title: Ada and the Oath
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, epilogue. Years later, a woman called Ada runs a small kitchen at the edge of the fae road, feeding travelers of both kinds, keeping one private book of names freely given. Corvane finds her by following nothing but love. The closing beat is homecoming: memory chosen, not traded; a story that belongs to its keeper.
